sources.news_title: Trump’s UFC Pal Could Be Headed for the White House Podium After His Desperate Search to Replace a Five-Day Flop
sources.text:
President Donald Trump appears ready to turn the White House briefing room into his personal UFC Octagon.
After two press secretaries and a bruising midterm, the president has turned to an unlikely candidate to defend him.
Vice President JD Vance stepped up on Sept. 3, leading the first briefing after Karoline Leavitt’s departure. Secretary of State Marco Rubio attempted to take her place in another briefing and her official replacement only lasted five days.
Still, the search for a permanent spokesperson drags on as familiar faces are running short.
Now, Trump seems convinced that someone accustomed to managing bruising confrontations might be just what his administration needs.
Trump Blows the Lid Off Katie Zacharia’s Short White House Run, From Podium Debut to Her Final Crash
Unfortunately for the president, his latest choice carries some baggage that critics have no intention of letting him forget.
On Saturday, Nov. 7, Trump announced on Truth Social that he had offered UFC CEO Dana White the job of White House press secretary.
Calling his longtime friend a “violent fighter and warrior,” Trump proposed bringing six MMA stars along as assistants, including Khabib Nurmagomedov, Justin Gaethje and Amanda Nunes.
“We need these people to defend us against the Lunatic Left,” he wrote, before pleading, “Dana, please take the job!”
White seemed happy to play along. He posted an altered Instagram image of himself behind the briefing room podium with the caption, “On to the next chapter.”
Neither White nor the administration confirmed whether the offer was serious, leaving Washington to wonder whether Trump was announcing an appointment or casting another reality show.
Social media users were hardly impressed with the president’s latest recruiting strategy.
“Good lord… he makes this country a laughingstock,” one person declared. Another added, “I think Trump is kidding, but is he? What does Dana White know about the workings of the administration? He’ll be answering ‘I’ll get back to you’ 99% of the time.”
One person simply snapped, “Trump’s lost his mind.”
More piled on jokes about Trump turning his presidency into a locker-room punchline and treating fighters as his press aides.
Someone else joined the discourse: “And you wonder why we got humiliated Tuesday. He never learns.”
Trump’s affection for White is hardly a recent development.
Their relationship dates back more than two decades, when Trump’s Atlantic City casino hosted UFC events that mainstream venues were unwilling to stage. White has returned that loyalty, speaking at three Republican National Conventions.
Their friendship reached another level on June 14, when White helped transform the White House South Lawn into an elaborate fighting arena for Trump’s 80th birthday celebration.
The multimillion-dollar UFC spectacle drew criticism over its enormous temporary arena, celebrity guest list and coveted seating arrangements. While wealthy executives enjoyed prime access, critics questioned whether the historic grounds had become another exclusive playground for Trump’s high-profile friends.
Even the president’s grand entrance became an unexpected attraction. Viral footage showed Trump reaching toward White during their lengthy walk to the Octagon, sparking speculation about whether he needed assistance. Although the footage did not establish that Trump was losing his balance, the moment quickly became a topic of online discussion.
However, Trump’s latest announcement revived another video involving White, and this one was considerably more troubling.
Footage from a December 2022 New Year’s Eve celebration in Cabo San Lucas, Mexico, showed White’s wife, Anne, slapping him during an argument before he slapped her back.
White later issued a public apology, acknowledging that there was no excuse for striking a woman. Despite calls for his removal, he remained in his position as UFC president, and the controversy eventually faded from public attention.
Meanwhile, Trump’s communications operation has its own revolving door. Leavitt departed in August, and her successor, Katie Zacharia, left after just five days in October.
After Republican midterm losses, Trump also named Stephen Miller to replace Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff.
Leavitt called Miller the “perfect choice” and praised Wiles as one of the “kindest and toughest” people she knew. Her remark that it was time to “fix what’s not working” was striking from someone who once vigorously defended the administration from the podium.
Wiles stayed gracious, calling her time serving Trump the “honor of a lifetime,” even as questions swirled about her exit.
For a president trying to regain control of the narrative, putting a fight promoter in the briefing room would guarantee another round of headlines.
But with his communications team in flux, critics may wonder whether Trump needs someone who can answer tough questions or simply another loyalist willing to step into the ring for him.

WEST PALM BEACH, Fla. — President Donald Trump said Saturday that he has offered the job of White House press secretary to his friend and UFC boss Dana White, an announcement unconventional even for the norm-busting president and one that nobody in the White House immediately confirmed.
Trump, while he was at his golf club in Florida, posted on social media that he made the offer to “the Great Dana White, a violent Fighter and Warrior” to become the Republican president’s chief spokesperson.
Trump said he requested that White bring along several UFC fighters as “assistants,” adding, “We need these people to defend us against the Lunatic Left. Dana will be a Press Secretary like none other. Dana, please take the job!”
The White House did not respond Saturday to messages inquiring about the Truth Social post.
White was in London on Saturday for a boxing event. A spokesperson for UFC did not immediately respond to messages seeking comment.
The UFC head shared an image of Trump’s post on Instagram, along with an image of himself standing behind the podium in the White House press briefing room with the words “On to the next chapter.”
Trump’s post came as his White House is in a period of major transition and struggling with his party’s deep losses in Tuesday’s midterm elections. The historic wins by Democratic candidates, including in areas that Republicans had held for decades, led to the GOP losing control of both chambers of Congress.
Trump on Friday announced he was replacing his longtime adviser Susie Wiles, who was seen as something of a tempering force on the president’s impulses, with aide Stephen Miller to serve as the next chief of staff. Miller is known as the architect of the administration’s hard-line immigration policies and is among the most determined of Trump’s inner circle.
The shake-up at the heart of his administration follows the brief but tumultuous week when Trump tried out a new press secretary in Katie Zacharia, who seemed uncomfortable in her sole appearance before reporters before leaving the job after five days.
The post had been vacant since Karoline Leavitt left at the end of August. Trump remains without a chief spokesperson.
Trump is close friends with White and has attended several UFC events with him since returning to the White House in January 2025.
He brought White and the sport to the White House’s South Lawn in June for the celebration of America’s 250th year of its independence and the president’s own 80th birthday. A wire-mesh Octagon was constructed near the executive mansion under ” The Claw,” a spaceship-like metal arch fitted with lights, sound equipment and large screens.
“It was an amazing experience, this was a one-of-one,” said White afterward.
White also spoke at the Republican National Conventions in 2016, 2020 and 2024.

Trump Offers Dana White White House Press Secretary Job
sources.text:
President Trump has offered UFC chief Dana White the White House press secretary role and urged him to bring top fighters as assistants, putting a longtime ally at the center of a restless communications shop.
President Donald Trump posted the offer on Truth Social and cast Dana White as the kind of fighter he wants at the podium after recent turnover in the press secretary post.
Fox News reported the Nov. 7 post and the president’s pitch: White would arrive as a “violent Fighter and Warrior,” with several UFC stars named as possible assistants to help “defend us against the Lunatic Left.”
Whether White takes the job remains unclear. He reposted Trump’s message, shared an image of himself behind the press briefing podium with the caption “on to the next chapter,” and is set to meet the president in the Oval Office on Monday, according to reporting carried by multiple outlets.
In the post, Trump framed the choice as a call for toughness at the daily briefings and made the ask personal.
He wrote on Truth Social:
"I am pleased to announce that the Great Dana White, a violent Fighter and Warrior, has been offered the job of Press Secretary of the United States."
Trump also listed the assistants he wanted White to bring, even noting some are not from the United States: Islam Makhachev, Khabib Nurmagomedov, Justin Gaethje, Daniel Cormier, Amanda Nunes, and Kayla Harrison.
He closed with a direct appeal:
"We need these people to defend us against the Lunatic Left. Dana will be a Press Secretary like none other. Dana, please take the job!"
Just the News reported the same offer language and the Monday White House meeting, along with White’s podium photo signaling interest in a new chapter.
The offer lands after a stretch of short tenures at the microphone.
Karoline Leavitt, who served as press secretary from the start of Trump’s second administration, announced her resignation in August and stepped down to focus on being a mother after welcoming a daughter earlier this year.
Katie Zacharia then held the job for about five days before Trump removed her last month, after a first press conference and interview that reporting described as a disaster. Her run was shorter than Anthony Scaramucci’s famous 11 days as White House communications director in 2017. Zacharia had earlier spent about six weeks as a communications adviser at Homeland Security.
On Oct. 23, Trump said he was in no rush to name a successor. The Dana White post put a high-profile name into that vacuum.
When a Daily Mail reporter called the White House for clarity on whether White would accept, the call was hung up.
White is no casual acquaintance. He is UFC’s president and CEO, a figure reported to be worth about $500 million, and one of Trump’s steadiest private-sector allies across campaign cycles and corporate freeze-outs.
Their public history runs back to 2001, when the first UFC event under White’s leadership was held at the Trump Taj Mahal in Atlantic City. Trump later called it the most unbelievable thing he had ever seen.
In 2016, Trump asked White to speak at the Republican National Convention. White did it despite people around him pleading that he refuse. White later told TIME what those warnings sounded like.
"Everybody said, \"Don't do it. Don't do it.\""
He added that the bigger objection was not politics alone: people insisted Trump would never win. White’s answer was blunt friendship first.
"It was about more than \"You don't want to get into politics.\" The bigger one was \"He's never gonna win.\" And I was like, \"Well, whether he wins or not, the guy's been a good friend to me.\""
After January 6, 2021, many corporations and celebrities distanced themselves from Trump. White did not. He kept Trump visible at UFC arenas when that choice carried a cost in elite circles.
On February 20, 2020, White appeared with the president in Colorado Springs ahead of a “Keep America Great” rally. On November 6, 2024, he spoke at Trump’s election-night event at the Palm Beach Convention Center. Earlier this year, UFC 250 was staged at the White House, another marker of how far the relationship had come.
Trump has credited White with opening doors to younger audiences the traditional political class does not reach.
In a TIME interview, Trump praised White’s presence on a stage.
"He's a very good speaker, very inspirational-type speaker. I know guys who are successful, they can't speak."
On White’s 2024 role, Trump was more specific: the UFC boss introduced him to people he had never heard of, including young interviewers and influencers. Trump said the help mattered.
“Very important. He introduced me to people I never heard of, young kids,” Trump said, describing sessions with 20-year-olds and asking, “Where the h*** did you meet these people?” He called them influencers with real audiences and said everything helps.
Reporting tied that network to names familiar to sports and podcast listeners, including the Nelk Boys, Will Compton, Taylor Lewan, Adin Ross, Theo Von, and Joe Rogan, the kind of non-cable pipeline that reached voters the press corps often misses.
White has also drawn a line around his own ambitions. In November 2024 he said he had no personal political aspirations. That earlier stance is why the press secretary offer, and his “next chapter” post, drew so much attention. A man who built a combat sports empire is now weighing a job defined by daily confrontation with the White House press corps.
TMZ reported White is scheduled to meet Trump in the Oval Office on Monday to discuss the role. White’s Instagram Story, the podium photo plus a repost of Trump’s message, read as interest without a final yes.
The mechanics of the “offer” still sit mostly on the social post and follow-up reporting. No formal personnel paperwork is detailed in the coverage. The White House has not given a clean public confirmation beyond the president’s own words and the planned sit-down.
What is clear is the pattern Trump is answering. Leavitt left. Zacharia lasted days. Midterms pressure is already part of the political weather. Trump’s fix is not another career flack. It is a loyalist who has stood with him when corporate America flinched, who can talk to young men through fight cards and podcasts, and who treats a hostile briefing room like a cage match instead of a seminar.
If White takes the job, the podium will sound less like institutional Washington and more like the people who actually show up to work, fight, and keep their word when the cameras turn mean.

US President Donald Trump on Saturday said he was asking mixed martial arts promoter Dana White to be the new White House press secretary. Trump has repeatedly tried to hitch his MAGA brand of politics to White's enormously successful Ultimate Fighting Championship.
US President Donald Trump said Saturday that he was offering a press secretary role to martial arts media magnate Dana White.
"I am pleased to announce that the Great Dana White, a violent Fighter and Warrior, has been offered the job of Press Secretary of the United States," Trump wrote on his Truth Social account. "Dana, please take the job!"
While White did not explicitly accept the job, the Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) boss posted a photo – possibly AI-generated – that showed him behind the lectern in the White House press briefing room, captioned "On to the next chapter."
The White House has been without a press secretary since October 16 when Katie Zacharia left the position after less than a week on the job.
White, 57, is president and CEO of the UFC, the largest and most successful organization in the world of mixed martial arts. UFC's violent cage fights are broadcast across the globe.

"We need these people to defend us against the Lunatic Left," Trump wrote.
The White House amplified the announcement by publishing a screenshot of the president's post on one of its official accounts.
Trump and White are old friends, and Trump has often tried to associate his MAGA brand of politics with the hugely popular UFC.
On his 80th birthday in June, UFC held a bloody cage match on the White House South Lawn. He has also attended bouts in Miami, New York and New Jersey since winning his second White House term.
When Trump won reelection in 2024, White appeared alongside the Republican for his victory speech.

Any hope that Donald Trump would respond to the Republicans’ midterms wipeout by quietly redecorating the White House and trying strike deals with his Democratic “friends” died on Friday when he announced that Stephen Miller would be the new White House chief of staff.
But rest assured that Trump’s lame-duck years won’t be totally focused on enacting cruel policies and seeking revenge on his enemies either. There’s also going to be plenty of previously unfathomable absurdity, as evidenced by Trump’s Saturday afternoon announcement on Truth Social that he wants Dana White to be his next press secretary:
While one aide told CNN that the president was joking, White House communications director Steven Cheung promoted his post on X:
White is Trump’s good friend. Their business and political ventures have been deeply entwined for decades, culminating in White staging an Ultimate Fighting Championship event on the White House lawn for the president’s birthday last June.
But still, why would White walk away from his role as as UFC president and CEO to be White House press secretary? Well, maybe he wouldn’t. While Trump’s Truth Social declaration initially looks like a hiring announcement, he’s actually just publicly begging White to take the job. The post says he’s merely offered White the role, and closes by begging, “Dana, please take the job!”
Maybe White is so loyal to Trump that he would step away from his day job. Or perhaps he thinks jumping fully into one of the most difficult roles in politics — perhaps for as little as five days — isn’t great for business.
White’s account has been active on X and Instagram in the hours since Trump’s post went up, and he posted what appears to be an AI-generated photos of himself as White House press secretary with the caption “On to the next chapter” to Instagram Stories:

Whether he’s accepted or not, White is probably looking to add to the drama ahead of UFC Vegas 124, which takes place on Saturday. Tune in to tonight’s cage match to learn the identity of the next White House press secretary!
Another theory: this is all a huge mix up. Someone on Team Trump suggested hiring a different Dana White, a woman who’s actually highly qualified to serve as press secretary in a Republican administration. But Trump got confused and wound up publicly inviting his Dana White to take the role:
Whatever is actually going on here, it seems the next two years are going to be stupider than we could possibly imagine.

By yourNEWS Media Newsroom
WASHINGTON — President Donald Trump announced Saturday, Nov. 7, that he had offered UFC President and CEO Dana White the position of White House press secretary, calling on the longtime mixed martial arts promoter to bring several prominent fighters into the administration as assistants. The announcement comes as Trump reorganizes his senior leadership following Republican losses in the midterm elections, although White has not publicly confirmed that he will accept the position.
In a Truth Social post, Trump praised White’s combative personality and suggested the UFC executive would bring a different approach to the White House briefing room.
“I am pleased to announce that the Great Dana White, a violent Fighter and Warrior, has been offered the job of Press Secretary of the United States,” Trump wrote, according to Reuters.
The president also proposed an unusual roster of assistants drawn from professional mixed martial arts, naming Islam Makhachev, Khabib Nurmagomedov, Justin Gaethje, Daniel Cormier, Amanda Nunes and Kayla Harris.
“I have requested that he bring with him assistants, even though some are not from our Country, of Islam Makhachev, Khabib Nurmagomedov, Justin Gaethje, Daniel Cormier, Amanda Nunes, and Kayla Harris,” Trump wrote. “We need these people to defend us against the Lunatic Left.”
He concluded with a direct appeal to the UFC executive: “Dana will be a Press Secretary like none other. Dana, please take the job!”
Trump’s language left uncertainty about whether the proposal was a formal employment offer or a lighthearted public invitation. Neither White nor UFC parent company TKO Group Holdings had immediately provided confirmation that the executive intended to leave his position in professional sports.
White responded on Instagram by sharing an image depicting himself at the White House press briefing podium with the caption “On to the next chapter.” He also shared a screenshot of Trump’s announcement, according to TheWrap. The posts acknowledged the president’s proposal but stopped short of confirming a career move.
Trump and White have maintained a relationship spanning approximately 25 years, beginning when Trump hosted early UFC events at his Atlantic City casino. White subsequently became a prominent political supporter, endorsing Trump during his presidential campaigns and speaking at three Republican National Conventions.
Their association continued during Trump’s second term. On June 14, 2026, the UFC held an event on the White House South Lawn as part of celebrations marking the nation’s 250th anniversary. White has also appeared alongside Trump at public events, including an August gathering in Las Vegas where the president promoted his economic policies.
The proposal follows an extended period of turnover in the White House communications office. Karoline Leavitt, who became the youngest White House press secretary when Trump returned to office in January 2025, departed in August. Her successor, Katie Zacharia, was removed in October after serving approximately five days and conducting one brief press briefing.
According to Scripps News, Zacharia’s departure followed questions about her legal credentials, including her use of the title attorney despite not having passed the California bar examination. The press secretary position has remained vacant since her departure, leaving the administration without a permanent spokesperson responsible for conducting regular White House briefings.
Trump’s latest offer also comes one day after he announced that Stephen Miller would replace Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff beginning Monday, Nov. 9. The leadership changes follow the Nov. 3 midterm elections, which gave Democrats control of both chambers of Congress and increased pressure on the president to reconsider his administration’s political and communications strategies.
The White House press secretary serves as the administration’s principal public spokesperson, communicating presidential policies, responding to questions from journalists and coordinating official messaging. White’s experience centers on professional sports promotion, business management and public relations rather than government communications, making his potential appointment a departure from the position’s conventional professional background.
As of Saturday afternoon, the White House had not formally announced White’s appointment, and the UFC executive had not confirmed whether he would accept. Trump’s public invitation and White’s social media response leave the position’s future unresolved as the administration prepares for further personnel changes.

Trump Pitches UFC Chief Dana White for White House Press Secretary
The president’s mock appointment turns a longtime personal alliance into a political performance, complete with a proposed team of heavyweight MMA champions enlisted to take on the left
Donald Trump has turned the White House press secretary’s job into an unlikely UFC proposition. His candidate is Dana White, the league’s longtime president and a friend of more than 25 years. The offer, announced on Truth Social in a post laced with irony, came with a proposed staff drawn from the sport’s biggest names: Islam Makhachev, Khabib Nurmagomedov, Justin Gaethje, Daniel Cormier, Amanda Nunes and Kayla Harris.
Trump’s pitch was less a personnel announcement than a political stunt. Presenting White as a fearless fighter and warrior, the president urged him to assemble the team, acknowledging that some of the proposed recruits are not American citizens. Their purpose, he suggested, would extend well beyond handling questions from reporters.
“We need these people to defend us against the crazy Left,” Trump wrote, linking the imagined communications operation to the Republican defeat in the midterm elections. He promised that White would be a press secretary unlike any the White House had seen before, then closed with an emphatic plea: “Dana, please accept the job!”
The post came with its own visual staging. Trump shared photographs of the fighters alongside an image of White in a suit, standing behind a podium as if he had already taken up the position. The combination of a mock appointment, a ready-made roster of fighters and a staged portrait turned the announcement into a piece of political theater built around Trump’s longstanding association with combat sports.
That association is personal as well as political. White, 57, was born in Manchester, Connecticut, on July 28, 1969. He has attended several Republican conventions and has been among Trump’s most visible allies in the world of professional sports. Their relationship dates back more than 25 years. Speaking to ESPN last May, White described the president as “one of my best friends” and said their friendship grew stronger with each passing year.
White has also helped bring the UFC directly into Trump’s political orbit. On June 14, he organized a UFC event at the White House to mark the president’s 80th birthday.
The press secretary’s office has previously been held by Karoline Leavitt and, briefly, by Katie Zacharia. Trump’s post offered no indication of a formal change in personnel; its language and presentation framed White’s prospective appointment as a joke. But the choice of a longtime ally, and the fighters enlisted in the imagined communications team, gave the message a distinctly political edge.

White has previously dismissed the idea of political office, though he is close with Trump and has spoken on his behalf at the RNC in pervious years. Earlier this year, the UFC staged a one-of-a-kind event on the White House lawn, UFC Freedom 250. The event, by any measure, was a rousing success.
The idea of White as Press Secretary, however, is almost instantly doomed to failure, especially with the UFC CEO and President already divided between MMA, Zuffa Boxing, UFC BJJ, and PowerSlap.
Katie Zacharia was released from her role as Press Secretary under Donald Trump in October, just five days into the job. Previously, Karoline Leavitt held the role, from January 2025 to August 2026.

sources.news_title: Donald Trump Says He Offered Dana White The Press Secretary Job
sources.text:
Donald Trump says he has offered UFC boss Dana White the job of White House press secretary. The president made the statement in a November 7 Truth Social post that also proposed a supporting cast of MMA stars, but did not announce that White had accepted.
The offer follows their collaboration on the UFC’s White House event. Trump framed the proposed job around White’s toughness and suggested bringing several fighters into the administration with him.
Trump Names MMA Stars In His Pitch To Dana White
The proposed assistants were Islam Makhachev, Khabib Nurmagomedov, Justin Gaethje, Daniel Cormier and Amanda Nunes. The text also names “Kayla Harris”; the accompanying collage includes UFC fighter Kayla Harrison.
Trump acknowledged that some were not American and pitched the group as defenders against his political opponents on the left. He closed with a direct appeal to White:
“Dana will be a Press Secretary like none other. Dana, please take the job!”
The attached collage depicts White at a presidential lectern above pictures of the fighters. It illustrates Trump’s proposal; it is not a photograph documenting White taking office.
An Offer, Not A Confirmed Move Out Of The UFC
The post supplies no starting date, acceptance from White or details about a change to his UFC role. It also does not establish appointments for the proposed assistants. The message offers no explanation of what duties the suggested fighter assistants would perform.
TMZ reported November 7 that White was expected to meet Trump on Monday about the possible job, citing sources with direct knowledge.
CNN subsequently reported that White had declined the proposal, citing a source familiar with the matter. One aide told the network that Trump was joking about the offer. CNN said it had asked the White House and UFC for responses. That attributed report differs from the earlier expectation of a meeting; neither report establishes that White accepted the job.
White had already taken a prominent role in Trump’s political appearances before this proposal. In a September 2024 written interview with TIME, he discussed leaving a family vacation in Italy to introduce Trump at that year’s Republican National Convention. White described being chosen, with the family’s support, as a major personal honor. He traced their friendship to Trump’s interest in fights and willingness to host the UFC when other venues were reluctant. He also said Trump regularly asked about his family. That account explains their personal connection; it was given more than two years before Saturday’s offer.
Gaethje already has a public connection to the president outside this proposed lineup. Trump hosted Gaethje and his family at the White House following his UFC Freedom 250 title victory. That earlier visit provides context for his inclusion here, but it was not an appointment to an administration position.
Trump also publicly praised White’s work on UFC Freedom 250 on the White House grounds during official remarks in Las Vegas on August 5. He thanked the promoter, singled out Gaethje and celebrated the event’s setting. Those remarks documented his enthusiasm for the UFC partnership months before the press-secretary proposal.
